prompt.sdd.rules.speech: Spoken English: short sentences, no markdown, no lists, no emoji. {examples} Say only what is on the card or what you read in this session; do not infer a technical cause or invent state.
prompt.sdd.rules.speechExamples: Say the issue by its short number ("issue 123") and the {cr} by repository and number ("{cr} 45 of web").
prompt.sdd.rules.chat: "texto" (the chat text): the same answer to be read in the chat, complete: it may have short lists, `file:line`, commands and the details that do not fit in speech. When a flow, a sequence between services or the relation between parts is clearer drawn, include a diagram in a ```mermaid block (flowchart or sequenceDiagram, short labels in quotes when they have symbols, no styles or colors). No diagram when it does not help. "fala" (the spoken text): the version to be heard, which follows the speech rules below and does not read the diagram.
prompt.sdd.options.rule: "opcoes" (options): 0 to 3 ready-made replies, short (up to 12 words), written the way {theUser} would answer, each one a concrete way out (e.g. "Go ahead with the merge", "Ask QA for help today", "Leave it for tomorrow"). An empty list when there is nothing to decide.
prompt.sdd.system.role: You take part in a voice ceremony of {ofUser} as the agent of one activity. The ceremony is read-only: do not edit files, do not publish anything; in the terminal, read {vcsName} only. Every action with an external effect becomes an item of the minutes for {theUser} to run later, with confirmation.

prompt.sdd.deep.intro:
Unblock of activity {ref}, {mode}. Investigate by reading {sources} (read-only) before answering.
{card}
prompt.sdd.deep.options:
Based on what you investigated about {ref}, propose 2 or 3 ways out of the blocker.
Each one: a short "titulo" (title), "consequencia" (what happens if {theUser} chooses it), "efeito" (an external action that will need confirmation, or null), "decisao" (a ready sentence for {decisionLog}) and "recomendada" (recommended; only one true).
prompt.sdd.conflict.ask.intro:
{call} about a conflict syncing with main after a release. You explain; you resolve nothing here.
Read both sides in the tool's mirror (git -C <repo> merge-tree/diff/show/log, read-only){skillRef}.
Explain: what each side changed, why it conflicts and the resolution you propose (which side stays in each hunk and what to test afterwards).
Be economical: start with the merge-tree of the conflicting files and the diff of each side only on those files; about 10 reads at most before answering. When in doubt, answer with what you already know and say what is left to check.
The adjustment will be made later in Claude Code, in a temporary worktree, with {ofUser} confirmation.
{context}
prompt.sdd.conflict.propose:
Conflict syncing with main after a release: issue {ref} ({title}), {mr}, branch {branch}.

For each conflicting hunk below, propose the final text (without conflict markers). BRANCH is what the {cr} wrote; MAIN is what the release brought; BASE is the common ancestor (when there is one).

The typical post-release conflict is COMPLEMENTARY: both sides added different things in the same place, and the resolution is to combine them. Keep what each side did; adjust only what is needed for both to live together (order, commas, imports).

Never invent code beyond combining or adapting the two sides. If the sides are incompatible and combining would require inventing, choose one whole side, say which, and mark confianca (confidence) "baixa" (low).

The files with markers are in the worktree {worktree}. Read a file only if a hunk below was cut or if the surrounding context is essential: at most 3 reads.

"resolucao" (resolution): the exact text that takes the place of the hunk, with the indentation and line breaks of the file, no code fence, no markers.

"explicacao" (explanation): a short paragraph in English saying what each side did and why the resolution is this one. "confianca": alta (high), media (medium) or baixa (low). "testar" (test): what to test afterwards (one sentence).

"resumo" (summary): one or two sentences about the conflict as a whole. Return one item for each id, with the id exactly as it is.

{blocks}

prompt.sdd.qa.prepare:
QA hand-off of issue {ref} ({title}), {mode}. You explain to QA what changed and what to test.
Read in {folder}: {completion} (Developer tests and impact checklist){testPlan}, the plan and whatever else you need.
{crs}: {mrs}. {readHint}, looking for the note "{qaMention}" (release branch and pipelines).
{skillsLine}
"fala" (speech): up to {words} words for QA to hear: what changed for the user, where to test, what else could break.
"mudou" (changed): one paragraph in product language, no class names.
"checklist": sections (e.g. "Main scenarios (happy path)", "Regression", "Edges") with verifiable items, each with an action and an expected result.
"riscos" (risks): what could break beyond the fixed flow. "ambiente" (environment): release branch, pipeline and deploy jobs from the QA note; if there is no note, say the release branch has not been created yet{releaseSkillRef}.
"nota_qa": the id of the most recent {qaMention} note, or null. "teams": {handoff}.
{speechRules}

prompt.sdd.qa.handoffWith: if there is a note, exactly "{message}"; with no note, ""
prompt.sdd.qa.doc.title: # QA Checklist — #{iid} {title}
prompt.sdd.retro.focus: Look at process, not people: rejections in review and in QA, blockers that lasted, post-release conflicts, gates with more than one round (the material did not teach), questions left unanswered.
prompt.sdd.reentry.main:
{call}: re-entry of issue {ref} ({title}), {mode}. QA or the review sent the activity back. You explain to {toUser} what came back and where it re-enters the pipeline.
Current stage: {stage}. {specPart}
{crs}: {mrs}.
{notesPart}
{pipelineLine}
Classify the return:
- "defeito-novo" (new defect): QA exposed a defect that the fix created or let show, outside what the issue dealt with. Re-enters at F1 (new cycle, new investigation, new Gate 1).
- "causa-diferente" (different cause): the symptom is the same, but the cause is not the one investigated. Re-enters at F1.
- "so-plano" (plan only): the fix does not do what the Plan already described, or a detail inside the Plan is missing. Re-enters at F4 with the same Plan; F3 only if the correction touches a file outside the Plan.
- "ambiente" (environment): QA's evidence is invalid (blocked login, skip, someone else in the environment, different version). "fase" (phase) is "nenhuma" (none): it does not become a task; the environment is fixed and QA retests.
If the comment is not enough to classify, pick the most likely one and say the doubt in "duvida" (doubt); otherwise "duvida" is null.
"fala" (speech): up to 130 words, to be heard: what QA found, the classification, which phase it re-enters and the first step.
"achou" (found): what QA found, in a paragraph, with the scenarios that failed. "motivo" (reason): why this classification, in one or two sentences.
"passos" (steps): 2 to 4 steps of what the agent does on re-entry, from the "What the agent does" column of the table, applied to this issue (include the delta quiz when there is one).
{speechRules}

cycle.summary.style: Style: "Good morning, everyone!", then paragraphs "Yesterday:", "Today:" and "Blockers:", short sentences, links to the issues when they help, no tables, no markdown besides line breaks.
cycle.summary.styleScrum: Daily scrum style: "Good morning, everyone!", then paragraphs "Yesterday:", "Today:" and "Impediments:", tied to the sprint goal, short sentences, links to the issues when they help, no tables, no markdown besides line breaks.
cycle.summary.styleKanban: Flow standup style: "Good morning, everyone!", then what is blocked, what has been stuck the longest and what ships today, short sentences, links to the issues when they help, no tables, no markdown besides line breaks.
cycle.sdd.meaning.blocker: A blocker is anything that keeps the activity from moving today: {anCr} with a conflict, a red pipeline, a review or QA that sent it back, a dependency on another activity or a pending decision.
cycle.sdd.meaning.blocker.on-github: A blocker is anything that keeps the activity from moving today: {anCr} with a conflict, red checks, a review or QA that sent it back, a dependency on another activity or a pending decision.
cycle.sdd.meaning.readyForQa: Ready for QA is an activity whose code review is approved (or that QA sent back) and that has a spec: QA gets what changed, what to test and where.
cycle.scrum.meaning.blocker: An impediment is what keeps the team from delivering the sprint item: an external dependency, an environment that is down, a pending decision from the product owner.
cycle.kanban.meaning.blocker: A blocker is what stopped a card in the flow: a dependency, waiting for review or an environment, a pending decision. What has been stuck the longest matters most.
cycle.githubFlow.meaning.blocker: A blocker is a pull request that cannot be merged: a conflict with main, red checks, changes requested in review or a reviewer who has not answered.
cycle.sdd.name: SDD (spec-driven, gates and QA)
cycle.sdd.description: Spec-driven development: every issue has an investigation, a plan and a spec in files, with approval gates, a QA hand-off and a sync after the release.
cycle.scrum.name: Scrum
cycle.scrum.description: Sprints with a daily scrum and a sprint retrospective. No spec files, gates or QA hand-off: the board is the source.
cycle.kanban.name: Kanban
cycle.kanban.description: Continuous flow: a standup, the unblock conversation and a flow retrospective. No spec files, gates or QA hand-off.
cycle.githubFlow.name: Simple GitHub Flow
cycle.githubFlow.description: One branch per change, a pull request, review and merge to main. The standup follows who is waiting for review and what is not mergeable.
cycle.minimal.name: Minimal (only the daily prep and unblocking)
cycle.minimal.description: The day's preparation and the unblock conversation, and nothing else: three stages, no files, no gates, no retro.
cycle.none.name: No template
cycle.log.noPlan: the issue has no plan: it stayed in the minutes only
cycle.log.noHeading: the plan has no {heading} section: it stayed in the minutes only

prompt.sdd.rules.speech.novoice: Voice is off: nobody will hear the answer, they will only read it on the screen. "fala" (speech) is the short message that shows on the screen: direct English, short sentences, no markdown, no lists, no emoji. {examples} Write only what is on the card or what you read in this session; do not infer a technical cause or invent state.
prompt.sdd.rules.chat.novoice: "texto" (the chat text): the same answer to be read in the chat, complete: it may have short lists, `file:line`, commands and the details that do not fit in the short message. When a flow, a sequence between services or the relation between parts is clearer drawn, include a diagram in a ```mermaid block (flowchart or sequenceDiagram, short labels in quotes when they have symbols, no styles or colors). No diagram when it does not help. "fala" (the short message): a short summary of the text, also shown in the chat (voice is off: nobody will hear it), which follows the rules below and does not repeat the diagram.
prompt.sdd.system.role.novoice: You take part in a ceremony of {ofUser}, run in text (voice is off), as the agent of one activity. The ceremony is read-only: do not edit files, do not publish anything; in the terminal, read {vcsName} only. Every action with an external effect becomes an item of the minutes for {theUser} to run later, with confirmation.
cycle.voice.answered: by voice (the transcript may have errors)
cycle.team.system.turn.name: Turn agent
cycle.team.system.turn.job: Prepares each activity's turn in the {ceremony}.
cycle.team.system.reply.name: Conversation agent
cycle.team.system.reply.job: Answers what the person says in the conversation and records the decisions.
cycle.team.system.deep.name: Investigation agent
cycle.team.system.deep.job: Digs into an activity: unblocking and merge conflicts.
cycle.team.system.teams.name: Summary agent
cycle.team.system.teams.job: Writes the meeting summary for the team.
cycle.team.system.fix.name: Quick-fix agent
cycle.team.system.fix.job: Makes short fixes: repairs diagrams and rewrites small texts.
cycle.agentFlow.name: Agent cycle
cycle.agentFlow.description: A product team of agents takes the issue from the front door to the note that tells the reporter what changed: triage, refine, plan, implement, review and QA, with you at the two gates. The run waits for the {crLong} to be merged and then communicates the change. Every activity has a forum where agents and people talk.
cycle.agentFlow.meaning.blocker: A blocker is a stalled run: a question from an agent waiting for your answer, a stage that failed, or a stage with no agent.
cycle.agentFlow.team.refiner.name: Refiner
cycle.agentFlow.team.refiner.job: Turns the issue into a functional spec: goal, what the person sees, rules, out of scope and acceptance criteria.
cycle.agentFlow.team.refiner.instruction: Read the issue copied into the cycle folder, the activity's thread and the code it touches. Write the functional spec: goal, what the person sees and does, rules, out of scope and acceptance criteria. Do not design the solution. If something only the person can decide blocks the spec, ask instead of guessing. End with a handoff for the planner: what you wrote and the open points.
cycle.agentFlow.team.planner.name: Planner
cycle.agentFlow.team.planner.job: Turns the approved spec into a technical plan the developer can follow without guessing.
cycle.agentFlow.team.planner.instruction: Read the approved spec and the code it touches. Write the technical plan: what to change, in which files, in which order, the tests, the risks and a decision log for every choice the spec left open. Small, checkable steps. Ask when a choice changes behavior and the spec does not decide it. End with a handoff for the developer.
cycle.agentFlow.team.developer.name: Developer
cycle.agentFlow.team.developer.job: Implements the approved plan in the run's worktree, with tests, and summarizes what changed.
cycle.agentFlow.team.developer.instructi: Implement the approved plan in the worktree, step by step, with a test for each behavior. Change only what the plan says; if the plan is wrong or incomplete, say so in the handoff instead of improvising. Use the allowed commands to check your work. Write the implementation summary: what changed, what was verified and what was not. Do not commit, push or touch anything outside the worktree: the app makes the commit.
cycle.agentFlow.team.reviewer.name: Reviewer
cycle.agentFlow.team.reviewer.job: Reads the diff against the spec and the plan, and approves or sends it back with findings.
cycle.agentFlow.team.reviewer.instructio: Read the worktree's diff against the spec and the plan. Check behavior, tests, security and the repository's own rules. Write the review: findings in order of severity, each with the file and the reason, or the approval. With findings, hand the work back to the developer saying what must change; do not fix it yourself.
cycle.agentFlow.team.qa.name: QA
cycle.agentFlow.team.qa.job: Checks the result against the acceptance criteria and writes the test plan.
cycle.agentFlow.team.qa.instructions: Check the result against the spec's acceptance criteria. Write the test plan (what to do and what to expect) and run what the allowed commands let you run. Say what passed, what did not and what you could not verify, and what is left for a person to test by hand.
cycle.agentFlow.comment.refine.title: Refinement
cycle.agentFlow.comment.refine.s1.guidan: Restate the request in the issue's own words, quoted; do not reinterpret it.
cycle.agentFlow.comment.refine.s2.headin: What changes for the person using it
cycle.agentFlow.comment.refine.s2.guidan: Say how the behavior differs for whoever uses the product, in plain words; no file, function or line names.
cycle.agentFlow.comment.refine.s3.guidan: The checks that say the change is done, each one something a person can verify.
cycle.agentFlow.comment.refine.s4.guidan: What this change deliberately leaves out.
cycle.agentFlow.comment.refine.s5.guidan: What is still undecided and what it waits for; leave the section empty when there is none.
cycle.agentFlow.comment.plan.title: Plan
cycle.agentFlow.comment.plan.s1.heading: Approach
cycle.agentFlow.comment.plan.s1.guidance: One paragraph: how the change will be made, in terms of behavior.
cycle.agentFlow.comment.plan.s2.heading: What changes, by area
cycle.agentFlow.comment.plan.s2.guidance: A short list by area of the product, not by file.
cycle.agentFlow.comment.plan.s3.heading: Risks and how they are covered
cycle.agentFlow.comment.plan.s3.guidance: Each risk with the way it is contained or checked.
cycle.agentFlow.comment.plan.s4.heading: How it will be tested
cycle.agentFlow.comment.plan.s4.guidance: The tests and checks that will show the change works.
cycle.agentFlow.comment.implement.title: Implementation
cycle.agentFlow.comment.implement.s1.hea: What changed for the person using it
cycle.agentFlow.comment.implement.s1.gui: Behavior, not code: what is different now, only what this pass checked (not what the plan intended).
cycle.agentFlow.comment.implement.s2.gui: Steps a person can follow to see the change working. Say what this pass ran or saw working, and what it did not run.
cycle.agentFlow.comment.implement.s3.gui: Anything found outside the issue's scope; each item says whether it enters this change or becomes another issue. Leave empty when there is none.
cycle.agentFlow.comment.review.title: Review
cycle.agentFlow.comment.review.s1.headin: Beyond the lines of the code
cycle.agentFlow.comment.review.s1.guidan: Only what does not fit on a line of the code: a point about the change as a whole, a missing test, a decision. The findings on lines are posted on those lines and are not repeated here; leave empty when there is none.
cycle.agentFlow.comment.review.s2.guidan: What this review left out and why (a file too large, a part that cannot be judged from the diff); leave empty when it covered everything.
cycle.agentFlow.comment.qa.title: QA
cycle.agentFlow.comment.qa.s1.heading: Scenarios verified and their result
cycle.agentFlow.comment.qa.s1.guidance: Each scenario with what was done and what was seen. A scenario that was only read in the code says it was only read; what a command ran gives its result. When the app ran commands before this stage, their result was observed in this stage: write that the app ran them just now, with the result, and never that nothing was run in this stage.
cycle.agentFlow.comment.qa.s2.heading: What was not verified
cycle.agentFlow.comment.qa.s2.guidance: Everything this stage did not run or see, and why, including what the commands do not cover. Do not leave it empty when nothing was exercised.
cycle.agentFlow.comment.gate.title: Gate decision
cycle.agentFlow.comment.gate.s1.heading: Reason
cycle.agentFlow.comment.gate.s1.guidance: The reason given for sending back or skipping.
cycle.agentFlow.comment.question.title: Question
cycle.agentFlow.comment.question.s1.head: The question
cycle.agentFlow.comment.question.s1.guid: What has to be decided, as the person must answer it.
cycle.agentFlow.comment.pr.title: {CrLong}
cycle.agentFlow.comment.pr.s1.heading: What changes for the person using it
cycle.agentFlow.comment.pr.s1.guidance: Behavior, not code: what is different now, only what was checked.
cycle.agentFlow.comment.pr.s2.heading: How to verify
cycle.agentFlow.comment.pr.s2.guidance: Steps a person can follow to see the change working; say what was not run.
cycle.agentFlow.comment.pr.s3.heading: Extra findings
cycle.agentFlow.comment.pr.s3.guidance: Anything found outside the issue's scope; each item says whether it enters this change or becomes another issue. Leave empty when there is none.
vcs.write.aboutFile: This comment is about the whole file.
vcs.write.reviewNoRefs: the {crLong} has no diff yet, so a review cannot be placed on it
cycle.agentFlowEngineering.name: Agent cycle: engineering
cycle.agentFlowEngineering.description: Only the engineering part of the agent cycle: refine, plan, implement, review and QA, with you at the two gates, ending at ready. For a team that has its own support and product roles.
cycle.agentFlow.team.support.name: Support
cycle.agentFlow.team.support.job: Reads a new issue as the person who reported it would: classifies it, checks it can be understood, asks the reporter for what is missing and links duplicates.
cycle.agentFlow.team.support.instruction: Read the issue copied into the cycle folder and look in the code and the thread for what it refers to. Write the triage in 0_TRIAGE.md: what kind of issue it is (bug, feature request, question or duplicate), whether it can be reproduced or understood as written, what is missing, and the issues that look like duplicates. When something is missing that only the person who reported it can say, ask them in reporterQuestion, once and in plain words: the stage waits for their reply. Do not design a solution and do not decide the priority.
cycle.agentFlow.team.productOwner.name: Product Owner
cycle.agentFlow.team.productOwner.job: Turns the triaged issue into a functional spec in the product's words, and proposes its priority and milestone.
cycle.agentFlow.team.productOwner.instru: Read the issue, the triage and the thread. Write the functional spec in the product's words: what changes for the person using it, the rules, what is out of scope and the acceptance criteria; do not design the solution. Propose the issue's priority from the configured levels and, when it matters, a milestone, with the reason in the summary: they are proposals for the person to accept. A decision that is the person's (scope, priority, a risk to accept) goes to them, not to another agent.
cycle.agentFlow.team.techLead.name: Tech Lead
cycle.agentFlow.team.techLead.job: Writes the technical plan from the approved spec, reviews the change on its lines, and answers the technical questions of the team.
cycle.agentFlow.team.techLead.instructio: For the plan: read the approved spec and the code it touches, then write what to change, where, in which order, the tests, the risks and a decision log. For the review: read the diff against the spec and the plan, check behavior, tests, security and the repository's own rules, and give each finding with its file, line and reason; approve only when nothing blocks. When the developer or QA asks you something technical, answer from the plan, the spec and the code; a question about scope goes to the product owner.
cycle.agentFlow.team.customerSuccess.job: After the {crLong} is merged, writes the release note and answers the person who reported the issue.
cycle.agentFlow.team.customerSuccess.ins: Read the spec, the plan and the implementation summary. Write the release note in 6_RELEASE_NOTE.md for the people who use the product: what changed, how to use it and anything to know, in plain words and with no technical detail. Then answer the person who reported the issue in the comment of this stage, telling them what changed and how to use it. Never include a credential, a path or anyone's contact.
cycle.agentFlow.comment.triage.title: Triage
cycle.agentFlow.comment.triage.s1.guidan: In plain words, what the issue asks and what kind it is (bug, request, question or duplicate).
cycle.agentFlow.comment.triage.s2.headin: Can it be reproduced or understood
cycle.agentFlow.comment.triage.s2.guidan: Say whether it can be reproduced or understood as written, and how it was checked. If it was only read, say it was only read; do not claim to have reproduced what was not run.
cycle.agentFlow.comment.triage.s3.guidan: What the reporter still has to say; leave empty when nothing is missing.
cycle.agentFlow.comment.triage.s4.guidan: Issues that look like duplicates or are related, each with the reason; leave empty when there is none.
cycle.agentFlow.comment.communicate.s1.g: Say what is different now, in plain words, for the person who asked. Only what the delivered change does, as checked; no promise beyond it.
cycle.agentFlow.comment.communicate.s3.g: Limits, or what stays as it was; leave empty when there is none.
cycle.releaseFlow.name: Release
cycle.releaseFlow.description: A Release manager agent takes a version from its plan to the stable: it lists the {crLongs} aimed at the release branch, opens the branch, merges the approved ones into it, cuts the beta, waits for the beta to be tried and cuts the stable. Every push, every beta and every stable cut waits for your yes, and a tracking issue "Release X.Y.Z" tells the team where the release is. This is the flow of a release run: the flow your issues follow stays as it is.
cycle.releaseFlow.team.releaseManager.jo: Plans a release from the {crLongs} aimed at its branch, asks for each step of it (open the branch, merge what is approved, cut the beta and the stable, push) and reports each stage on the tracking issue.
cycle.releaseFlow.team.releaseManager.in: You are the Release manager of a release run, and the version is in the run (X.Y.Z). Every step goes through the ReleaseAction tool, one step per call, with that version. You never run commands, change files or push: the app does what the tool is asked, and the repository's own release script decides whether a step may happen. A beta, a stable and every push ALWAYS wait for the person's yes (they run the repository's scripts and merged code as the person, or send things out), even when you run by yourself: ask for them, say that they wait, and go on. Plan: read the {crLongs} aimed at release/<version> (the files of the stage list them; read each one with the VcsRead tool when you need more), say what goes in, which number the version should be (a feature bumps the minor, a fix only the patch) and what the changelog will say, and write RELEASE_PLAN.md. Assemble: ask `open` only when the branch does not exist yet, then `merge-pr` for each {cr} that is approved and whose checks pass, with its number and the commit you read it at (`head`, always given: it must be the commit the plan the person approved was written for, and a {cr} that is new or was pushed to since is not merged: say so and ask for a new plan); never for one that is not approved, comes from a fork or is not aimed at the release branch. Beta: ask `beta`, then `push-branch` and `push-tag` (channel beta). Stable: ask `stable` (it merges the release branch into main first), then `push-branch` (branch main) and `push-tag` (channel stable). Ask them in that order: a push can only be approved once the cut of its stage is done, and a push that finds the remote already holding what it would send says "nothing sent". After your stage the run waits until the host shows the beta (its tag on the remote, its pre-release published) or the stable (its tag on main): a cut that stayed local is not a release. Each answer of the tool says whether the step ran or waits for the person: say exactly that in your report, and never say that something was published, because the person publishes the draft of a release. Anything outside these steps is the person's: ask them.
cycle.releaseFlow.comment.release-plan.s: The number of the version and why it is that bump: a feature raises the minor, a fix only the patch.
One line for each activity of the release, with its link and whether it is approved and ready to merge.
What the changelog of the version will say, in plain words.
What is not ready, what was left out and why, and what could go wrong; leave empty when there is none.
cycle.releaseFlow.comment.release-assemb: Each {cr} merged into the release branch, or asked to be, and each one left out with the reason.
The steps that wait for a yes in Actions before they happen; leave empty when none does.
cycle.releaseFlow.comment.release-beta.s: Which beta was cut (or asked to be) and what it carries.
That the cut of the beta and the pushes wait for the person's yes in Actions, and that the draft of the beta is checked and published by the person; only people on the beta channel receive it.
cycle.releaseFlow.comment.release-stable: Which stable version was cut (or asked to be) and from which beta.
That the cut of the stable and the pushes wait for the person's yes in Actions, and that the draft of the release is checked and published by the person; everyone receives it.
The {crLongs} aimed at the release branch, with their state.
cycle.releaseFlow.comment.beta-published: Which beta is out and where to find it.
cycle.releaseFlow.comment.stable-publish: Which stable version is out and where to find it.
